name: Dayao Yi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: ISO code retired 2008, merged into Lipo [lpo]; no Dayao-Yi-specific description

sources.citation: Merrifield, W. Scott. 2012. Yao'an Central Yi Phonology. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2012-002. Sec. 4 'Syllable stress', p. 9.
sources.note: For Yao'an Lolo (Lolopo, the OTHER Central-Yi vernacular, not Lipo): 'Stress is not contrastive for Yao'an Central Yi... when there is a two-syllable utterance, the syllable with the higher tone carries slightly greater stress.' Not applicable to daya1245 but the nearest relative with an explicit statement.

sources.citation: Gao, Katie B. 2017. Dynamics of Language Contact in China: Ethnolinguistic Diversity and Variation in Yunnan. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Nothing (sociolinguistic). Sec. 2.4.2.2 distinguishes Eastern Lipo (Wuding, Lisu-classified) from 'Western Lipo (Yi) in Yongren'; cites an SIL survey report 'Yang and Flaming (2012)' on Lolo and Western Lipo that is absent from her bibliography.

sources.citation: Hayashi, Norihiko 2015. A phonological sketch of Lolopo (RIHN Descriptive Linguistics 7).
sources.note: grep of text layer: no mention of Lipo, stress or accent (Lolopo, not Lipo).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Jamin R. Pelkey, supported by David Bradley). 2007. Change Request 2007-073: retire [yio] 'Lipo, Western' and merge into [lpo] Lipo (adopted 2008-01-14). Dallas: SIL International. 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Establishes identity only: [yio] (Western Lipo, Yi-nationality Lipo) and [lpo] (Eastern Lipo, Lisu-nationality Lipo) are 'mutually intelligible dialects of the same language' per Bradley's fieldwork.

sources.citation: Yu, Defen. 2007. Aspects of Lisu phonology and grammar, a language of Southeast Asia. Pacific Linguistics 588. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 3.6 'Phonemic system of Lipo' (Lipo of Luquan County), pp. 62-65.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Offsite Storage PL4001.L61 Y8 2007
sources.note: Silent on stress. States Lipo syllable = C V T and that Lipo 'distinguishes only four tones' (55, 33, 21, 21 creaky/glottal); consonant and vowel inventories; no word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the phonology chapter scanned.

sources.citation: Bradley, David et al. 2006. Southern Lisu Dictionary. STEDT Monograph 4. Berkeley. Introduction pp. xvi-xvii.
sources.note: Nothing on Lipo prosody; demography only ('The Lipo number over 250,000, of whom over 60 per cent, mainly in Yongren, Dayao, Yao'an and western Yuanmou... are classified as members of the Yi nationality').

sources.citation: Bradley, David. 2017. Lisu. In G. Thurgood & R. LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages, 2nd ed., 902-917. London: Routledge. (1st ed. 2003: 222-235)

sources.note: Bradley is the fieldworker on Lipo dialects named in the ISO merge; his Lisu chapter treats Lipo ('Eastern Lisu') and is the most authoritative English overview that might comment on prosody.

sources.citation: Mu Yuzhang 木玉璋. 2002. 傈颇话概况 [Lipohua gaikuang / A brief description of Lipo]. Minzu Yuwen 民族语文 2002(4): 68-80.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only published stand-alone sketch of Lipo (Glottolog's grammar_sketch for lipo1242); its 语音 section is the most likely place for any remark on 轻重音/stress or its absence. Describes Wuding/Luquan (Eastern) Lipo, mutually intelligible with Dayao Lipo per ISO CR 2007-073.

sources.citation: Fan Junjun 范俊军 & Mahai Buji 马海布吉. 2019. 会理彝族俚泼话音系及系属. Guizhou Minzu Yanjiu 贵州民族研究 40(3): 166-174.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Systematic phonology of a Yi-nationality (Western-type) Lipo variety with explicit comparison to Chuxiong Lipo; a full 音系 description may state syllable prominence/stress.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn & Flaming, (?) 2012. [Sociolinguistic survey report on Lolo and Western Lipo, Chuxiong Prefecture]. SIL East Asia Group survey report (cited as 'Yang and Flaming 2012' in Gao 2017: 32; not in her bibliography).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only known survey specifically covering Western Lipo (= Dayao/Yongren Yi, the yio referent); SIL survey reports usually carry a phonology appendix.

sources.citation: Chen Kang 陈康. 2010. 彝语方言研究 [A study of Yi dialects]. Beijing: Zhongyang Minzu Daxue Chubanshe. 634 pp.

sources.note: Covers the Central dialect (中部方言) with Lipo 里泼 and Lolopo vernacular phonologies from Chuxiong (Dayao/Yongren/Yao'an) datapoints; Chinese dialect monographs of this type sometimes include a line on 重音/轻声.

sources.citation: Zhu Wenxu 朱文旭. 2005. 彝语方言学 [Yi dialectology]. Beijing: Zhongyang Minzu Daxue Chubanshe. 430 pp.
